pvwatts_system_loss_pct.rationale: Percent system losses passed to PVWatts per shading level. 14% is the PVWatts default; 20% and 30% are product choices for some and heavy shading, not measured values.

target_offset.rationale: Share of annual usage the recommended system aims to cover. Product choice: size to roughly 90-100% of usage.

system_size_cap_kw.rationale: Upper limit on recommended system size so very large bills do not produce unrealistic rooftop systems. Product choice.

min_system_size_kw.rationale: Below this recommended size the calculator warns that the bill may be too small for solar to make financial sense (fixed installation overhead dominates). Product choice, not a sourced threshold; the system is not resized, only a warning is shown.

panel_degradation_per_year.rationale: Annual loss in panel output used in the 25-year projection. Product choice (0.5% per year).

analysis_years.rationale: Length of the net-savings projection. Product choice (typical panel warranty length).

ca_self_consumption_share.rationale: Share of solar output used on site (valued at the retail rate) versus exported at the lower net billing credit, for California homes. Placeholder product choices pending owner review; batteries raise self-consumption.

annual_rate_escalation.rationale: Yearly growth in the retail electricity rate used in the 25-year projection. Product choices, not sourced facts. Florida: no primary source gives a forward forecast, so 2/3/4% is a choice around general inflation; for context EIA reports a Florida residential average of 14.14 cents/kWh in 2024 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/sales_revenue_price/pdf/table_5A.pdf). California: the Public Advocates Office (CPUC) Q2 2026 Electric Rates Report, PDF page 8 (https://www.publicadvocates.cpuc.ca.gov/-/media/cal-advocates-website/files/press-room/reports-and-analyses/260727-public-advocates-office-q2-2026-electric-rates-report.pdf), prints residential average rate increases from January 2016 to June 2026 of +69% (PG&E), +101% (SCE) and +97% (SDG&E). Over those 10.5 years the compound rate is (1 + total change)^(1/10.5) - 1, about 5.1%, 6.9% and 6.7% a year (our arithmetic). The CPUC's 2025 SB 695 report, PDF page 6 (printed page 2) (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/-/media/cpuc-website/divisions/office-of-governmental-affairs-division/reports/2025/2025-sb-695-report_093025.pdf), prints about 11%, 8% and 7% a year for PG&E, SCE and SDG&E over 2016-2024, and a 2025-2028 forecast of about 6% a year for PG&E and SDG&E and about 7% a year for SCE. The report's footnote 14 defines these as simple averages (total change divided by years), not compound rates. The California range is 3% (low), 4.5% (likely) and 6% (high). The likely value sits below every utility's compound history above; the high value is above PG&E's 5.1% compound history but below SCE's 6.9% and SDG&E's 6.7% and close to the CPUC's 6-7% forecast. It is deliberately not higher because assuming the recent pace persists for 25 years is not defensible. Owner to review.

missing_range_spread.rationale: Placeholder spread used only when a sourced cost line has a likely (median) value but a null low and/or high bound (currently installed cost per watt in FL and CA, and the battery cost high end). The engine fills the missing bound as likely x (1 - spread) or likely x (1 + spread) and says so in the results' assumptions list. Product choice, not a sourced figure; it stops applying as soon as the owner fills the real bounds in costs.json.
